summary: SL-023 gave validate a way to read the published exe's own window without UI Automation. It added `--report <file>`, which writes schema-1 JSON read from the rendered controls after the first ending (exit codes 0/2/3/70); a reader script, eng/read-window.ps1; and a 12-case PowerShell suite, tests/window/WindowCases.ps1. Validate met all 14 criteria against a fresh publish of the real exe, including real trees and C:\Program Files. Three minor obligations (O-016 exit 0 without a file, O-017 an untested final-write failure, O-018 a false fitness.yaml header) were accepted-pending and are still unbuilt, so the slice reaches reflect with them open.

payload.summary: SL-023 gave validate a way to read the published exe's own window without UI Automation. It added `--report <file>`, which writes schema-1 JSON read from the rendered controls after the first ending (exit codes 0/2/3/70); a reader script, eng/read-window.ps1; and a 12-case PowerShell suite, tests/window/WindowCases.ps1. Validate met all 14 criteria against a fresh publish of the real exe, including real trees and C:\Program Files. Three minor obligations (O-016 exit 0 without a file, O-017 an untested final-write failure, O-018 a false fitness.yaml header) were accepted-pending and are still unbuilt, so the slice reaches reflect with them open.
payload.estimate_error: Right on defect severity, wrong on size, and the risk tier hid the slice's downstream weight. Medium/low produced 3 minors, no blocker, and validate found nothing new. But the size missed an unplanned 12-case harness, tests/window/WindowCases.ps1 (34 s for All, 24 s for C-002 alone), and three separate 300 MB SDK 10 bootstraps: two spike scratch clones plus the build worktree. Low risk skipped critique and critique-review on the slice that defines what every later screen slice (starting with the tree) can be verified by: schema 1, the exit-code table, add-never-rename and the reader. The design marked schema reversibility 'cheap', but the committed read-window.ps1 and WindowCases.ps1 now parse schema 1, so that flipped inside the slice. Nothing challenged whether four controls' Text is enough for a tree.

learned.lesson: A design that says 'no engine-run test discharges the App cases; validate's exe runs do' is overruled by the engine. `case` obligations are owed to build-slice with a runnable command, so the builder writes the harness anyway. The next App-touching design must name where each case's test lives and the command that runs it. Otherwise the harness is unplanned and no design gate reads it.
learned.evidence: Build deviation: 'The design said no engine-run test would cover the App cases... the case obligations are owed to build-slice with a runnable command, so I added tests/window/WindowCases.ps1'. O-004 to O-015 were all discharged there with model contact.

learned.lesson: The App's verification recipe is: publish through `pwsh -File eng/dotnet.ps1 publish src/FsAnalyser.App/FsAnalyser.App.csproj -c Release -o artifacts/publish`; read one root with `eng/read-window.ps1 -Root`; run cases with `tests/window/WindowCases.ps1 -Case <id|All>`. `dotnet test` runs only the 86 Core tests and never runs the window cases, so a tree-slice regression in MainWindow stays green unless that slice names WindowCases.ps1 in its own checks and adds cases to it. Report schema 1 has window (OutcomeTitle, OutcomeDetail[], CountersText, OutcomePanel{visible,actualHeight}) and core. It is written once, at the first ending only, and keys are add-never-rename.
learned.evidence: Code review and validate ran the three commands by hand. WindowCases.ps1 is not wired into the solution. WindowReport.cs header documents the schema. The design's 'EndingShown fires each time; only the App's handler keeps the first'.

learned.lesson: Scan time on this machine is driven by folder count, not file count. 30,000 empty files in 110 folders took 54 ms, and 30,150 folders plus 4,500 files took 1,589 ms (about 6 timer ticks). A case that needs many timer ticks needs tens of thousands of folders, and building that tree makes the case 24 s long. CountersText after the last tick lags the final total (28,350 vs 30,150), so no case may treat it as final. The tree slice's large-folder cases will hit the same sizing.
learned.evidence: Build deviation on C-002 (the spike used only 20-file trees, where no tick ever ran); WindowCases C-002 at 20,100 folders (1,039 ms) was enlarged to 30,150 (1,589 ms). Code review measured CountersText at 28,350 folders against a final 30,150.

learned.lesson: Validate drove the unmodified published exe in-process with DOTNET_STARTUP_HOOKS and a temp hook dll (FSA_HOOK_MODE=stop, throw or close). The guard allowed it. That is how it reached the Stopped ending, the exit-70 path, closed-early, and how it read the no-flag window and the pre-slice exe (dc5d607) as an observer-effect oracle. The hook lives in validate's %TEMP%, not in the repo, so the next validate must rebuild it, and no committed test covers those paths.
learned.evidence: Validate criteria 6 and 12 and the O-001 comparison ('read in-process by a startup hook'). Neither 'what it changed' nor tests/ contains a hook project. The build left C-006 and C-012 untested.

learned.lesson: Minor findings disposed accepted-pending do not spend a lap. Code-review #2 and validate passed with O-016 to O-018 unbuilt (build attempts = 1), and validate recorded two checks on them as 'failed' while still passing. Reflect is the only stage left that can carry them to the backlog. For every later slice, each accepted-pending minor at reflect must become a candidate or it is lost. Here that leaves the WindowReport.cs header's 'Exit 0: the report was written' and the fitness.yaml header both known to be false.
learned.evidence: Validate [failed] 'O-016: closing the window before the ending in report mode' and 'O-017 and O-018 addressed in the tree'. Code-review #2: '3 answered by a model... counted as untriaged'.

learned.lesson: On this low-tier slice critique and critique-review did not run, so the executing code-review was the whole safety net. It earned its cost by running two paths no test reached (window closed before the first ending; report folder deleted mid-scan) and reproducing a contract violation. Keep code-review with contact 'code' on App slices; a read-only review would have missed m1.
learned.evidence: Critique #1 and critique-review #1 were 'sized out' (none contact). Code-review #1: 'I also ran two paths no test reaches... exit 0 and no file. This contradicts the contract documented in WindowReport.cs.'

learned.lesson: The exit-code contract was repaired in one direction only. The design guaranteed 'every non-zero exit leaves no file' by deleting the target in the exit-70 handler. It never checked the converse, 'exit 0 implies a file'. App.xaml keeps the default ShutdownMode OnLastWindowClose, and WPF keeps the first Shutdown code, so closing the window early or an exception after Shutdown(0) both give exit 0 with no file. Any new exit path in report mode must be checked in both directions, and framework defaults (ShutdownMode) count as paths.
learned.evidence: m1 and O-016; coherence_check item (1) fixed only the exit-70-after-good-write half; code-review #1 reproduced closing at 517 ms on a 30,000-folder tree.

learned.lesson: Schema 1 exposes only OutcomeTitle, OutcomeDetail, CountersText and OutcomePanel. It does not expose UnreadableExpander, so the unreadable-folders list, which SL-020's counting rules make a first-class ending element, cannot be read from the window. The keys were derived from what ShowOutcome assigns, not from every named control visible at the ending. The tree slice should derive its keys from the screen's control list.
learned.evidence: Validate not-reached: 'C:\Program Files had 1 unreadable folder, but schema 1 does not expose UnreadableExpander'.

learned.lesson: tests/window/WindowCases.ps1 must stay ASCII-only, with non-ASCII test text built from escapes at run time. A tool write silently turned the test's own 'é' literals into real characters and C-010 then searched for the wrong text (the app was fine). Files the builder wrote also needed CRLF normalisation. The tree slice will add non-ASCII folder names to the same file.
learned.evidence: Build's [failed] first run of C-010 and the two Release builds 'before and after the CRLF normalisation'.

learned.lesson: Expect about 36 s and 300,608,304 bytes for the first dotnet command in every fresh worktree or scratch clone, because .dotnet/ is per-tree and gitignored. This slice paid it three times (two spike clones, the build worktree). Any spike that needs to build should reuse an existing .dotnet instead of re-running eng/dotnet.ps1. Size any slice that opens a new worktree with that in it.
learned.evidence: Spikes report-equals-final-rendered-window ('SDK 10.0.401 (300 MB) ... 37 s') and app-test-project-drives-mainwindow ('35.6 s'); build's 'First run downloaded SDK 10.0.401 (300,608,304 bytes)'.

what_went_wrong: Three owed minors (O-016 exit 0 without a file, O-017 an untested final-write failure, O-018 a false fitness.yaml header) went through code-review #2 and validate unbuilt. The slice reaches reflect with the WindowReport.cs header ('Exit 0: the report was written') and the fitness.yaml header both known to be false. Validate recorded checks on two of them as 'failed' and still passed.

The design decided that no engine-run test would cover the App cases, and the engine routes case obligations to build-slice with a runnable command. The builder had to invent tests/window/WindowCases.ps1 (12 cases) outside the design. With critique sized out, the harness's placement, its publish-if-stale logic and the republish race (flagged and still unfixed) were read by nothing before code review.

The design's C-002 shape ('thousands of files in nested folders') was wrong about what produces timer ticks: 30,000 files took 54 ms. The design admitted the spike used only 20-file trees, yet shipped an unmeasured size. The builder found it by measuring and enlarged the tree twice (20,100, then 30,150 folders).

Build-check halted on a slice whose every derived criterion was 'missing', which is the normal state of a slice that has not started, and ran twice. It also declined to run the tests although Q-003 already allowed the SDK download, leaving 'repo tests: unknown'. C2 (an alternative to C1) is still listed 'missing' in the loop's open list after validation passed, and it can never be satisfied.

Design-slice halted once on Q-016 (does 'nothing is saved to disk' cover an opt-in `--report` file?). The design had already chosen the file form and flagged the risk. A model answered in question-chat, confirmed it as written, and nothing changed. That was a whole lap to confirm an existing decision.

The engine appended the two SL-023 fitness entries before the build. They break three claims in the file's own header: xUnit twins, 'Five rules, eight entries', and single quotes with including_comments true. The design declared them 'only in .taad/fitness.yaml' without checking the header. Every later slice that declares rules (Q-010) will falsify it again.
The builder's first WindowCases run failed C-010 because a tool write changed the test's own 'é' literals into real characters. This was self-inflicted, not an app defect, and cost a run.

The three code-review findings were disposed by a model, not a person (counted as untriaged in that gate's precision), and all three were set to accepted-pending, so the reviewed record has no independent check of those dispositions.

missed.what: The design's exit table says 'Exit 0: the report was written', but the critique did not ask which code path produces each exit code, including framework defaults. App.xaml keeps ShutdownMode OnLastWindowClose, so closing the window before the first ending exits 0 with no file. WPF also keeps the first Shutdown code, so an exception after Shutdown(0) leaves exit 0 with the report deleted. The coherence check fixed only 'non-zero implies no file'. Critique was sized out on this low-risk slice, so this measures the skip.
missed.caught_by: code-review #1, by launching report mode on a 30,000-folder tree and closing the window 517 ms in (m1 / O-016)

missed.what: Case C-009's 'why' names both the startup delete and 'the final move' as failure points. Its shapes (a missing parent folder, or the path being a directory) already fail at the startup delete, so neither can reach the final-write catch in App.xaml.cs or the delete-and-rethrow in WindowReport.cs. A check would be: for every case row, name the line its shape reaches and confirm it is the one the 'why' names.
missed.caught_by: code-review #1, by deleting the report's parent folder after the window appeared mid-scan (m2 / O-017)

missed.what: Case C-002 assumed 'thousands of files in nested folders' scans across many 250 ms timer ticks. The design itself noted that the spike ran only 20-file trees and never measured scan speed. On this machine 30,000 files in 110 folders took 54 ms, and ticks need tens of thousands of folders.
missed.caught_by: build-slice, which measured 54 ms and enlarged the tree

missed.what: Key decision 'No xUnit App test project... validate's exe runs discharge the App cases' assumed validate discharges case obligations. The engine owes case obligations to build-slice with a runnable command. A check would be: for each case, which stage discharges it, and with what command?
missed.caught_by: build-slice, recorded as a deviation; the builder wrote WindowCases.ps1

missed.what: Schema 1's keys were taken from what ShowOutcome and ShowProblem assign, not from every named control visible at the ending. UnreadableExpander, the unreadable-folders list that SL-020's counting rules make first-class, is not in the report, so validate could not read it on C:\Program Files (1 unreadable folder).

The design put its two architecture rules 'only in .taad/fitness.yaml' with no xUnit twin. It did not check that the file's header promises a twin per entry, a fixed 'Five rules, eight entries' count, and single-quoted entries with including_comments true. The entries the engine appended break all three, and `dotnet test` stays green if MainWindow starts referencing WindowReport.

unknowns: Report mode fires once, at the first ending. How will it read a state reached by interaction, such as expanding a folder holding 100,000 virtualized items (U-001's under-0.5 s target)? Candidates are a startup-hook driver, an `--expand <path>` option, or a second report trigger. This has to be spiked on the real exe before the tree slice is designed, because schema 1 has no place for rows.

Does the window render, and does Dispatcher.Yield(Loaded) fire, when the person's session is locked, RDP-disconnected or the screen is off? The autopilot runs unattended in that state. O-002 was discharged only for an interactive session 1 on Windows 11 26200, and validate listed non-interactive, RDP and locked sessions as not reached.

How can the VolumeInUse/Coverage ending line and the real `C:\` argv repair be read end to end without the agent scanning the person's own drive under the machine guard? That would take a person's grant or a small dedicated volume, and no stage has shown either works. C-013 tested only a temp folder with a trailing backslash.

candidates.title: Close SL-023's three owed minors: exit 0 implies a file, a final-write-failure case, and the fitness.yaml header
candidates.why: O-016, O-017 and O-018 were accepted-pending and never built (build attempts = 1). Three edits: an Exit handler in StartReportMode that turns exit 0 with no file into a non-zero code, covering both the closed-early and the exception-after-Shutdown(0) paths, and documented in the WindowReport.cs header; a third Test-C009 run that deletes the report's folder once MainWindowHandle is non-zero and expects exit 3 with no file or .tmp; and a fitness.yaml header amendment that drops the fixed count and marks '# settled by SL-0xx' entries as Fitness-only.

candidates.title: Commit the DOTNET_STARTUP_HOOKS driver validate used, with stop, throw and close modes, under tests/window
candidates.why: Validate reached the Stopped ending (criterion 6), the exit-70 path (criterion 12) and closed-early through a temp hook dll that is not in the repo, so C-006, C-012 and O-016 have no committed test. The tree slice needs click and expand without UIA, and the guard allowed this route.

candidates.title: Add UnreadableExpander to report schema 1 (add-only) with a case that reads a non-empty unreadable list
candidates.why: Validate found 1 unreadable folder on C:\Program Files and could not read the list, because schema 1 has no key for it. Adding it is allowed by add-never-rename. A case with an ACL-denied temp folder would check the window against SL-020's unreadable-folder counting rule.

candidates.title: Fix design._append_rules so engine-appended fitness entries match the file's header and quoting, or write to a marked section
candidates.why: The two SL-023 entries broke the header's 'twin of ArchitectureRulesTests', its 'Five rules, eight entries' and its single-quote/including_comments conventions. Q-010 means every later slice appends more, so the header will be false again, and the tree slice will declare rules.

candidates.title: Build-check: stop halting when every derived criterion is missing on a slice with no attempts, and treat alternative criteria as one
candidates.why: Build-check #1 halted 'partial' on a greenfield slice and ran twice. Its C2 (an alternative to C1) can never be satisfied and stays 'missing' in the loop's open list after validation passed.

candidates.title: Let eng/dotnet.ps1 and spikes reuse one SDK 10 install across worktrees and scratch clones
candidates.why: The same 300,608,304-byte SDK 10.0.401 was downloaded three times in this slice at about 36 s each, because .dotnet/ is per-tree and gitignored. Every new slice worktree and spike clone pays it again. Q-003 chose the repo-local install, so a shared location needs the person's agreement.

candidates.title: Run the published exe with --report on a real drive root once, under a person's grant, and record the Coverage line
candidates.why: No test has read the VolumeInUse/Coverage third OutcomeDetail line or the real `C:\` argv repair from the window. Validate declined a drive-root scan so as not to read metadata across the person's folders.
